reconstructed_theorem_text: For every finite-dimensional real inner-product normed vector space E equipped with its Borel measurable structure, define S={w:E | norm_E(w)=1}, with the inherited topology and measurable structure. Write u_bar for the ambient representative of u in S. Define the actual real function c:S times S->R by c(u,v)=Real.arccos(inner_product_E(u_bar,v_bar)), using the principal real inverse cosine. Then c is jointly continuous for the product of the inherited topologies and is measurable for the product measurable structure. For every u,v in S, all six pairwise conclusions hold: 0<=c(u,v); c(u,v)<=pi; c(u,v)=InnerProductGeometry.angle(u_bar,v_bar); norm_E(u_bar-v_bar)<=c(u,v); c(u,v)=0 if and only if u=v as subtype points; and c(u,v)=c(v,u). For every u,v,w in S the triangle inequality c(u,w)<=c(u,v)+c(v,w) holds. In the angle formula, angle(a,b)=arccos(inner_product(a,b)/(norm(a)*norm(b))); because these representatives have norm exactly 1, that denominator is exactly 1. Thus no zero-denominator convention is needed when identifying the two displayed formulas on S, despite real division being totalized in general. Equality of subtype points is equality of their ambient representatives. The continuity, measurability, range, angle identity, chord comparison, zero characterization, symmetry and triangle inequality are all conclusions; no such property of c is assumed. No positive dimension or nonempty sphere is required. If E has dimension zero, S is empty, so pair and triple universal assertions are vacuous and the empty-domain function still has the asserted continuity and measurability. The theorem concerns this specific real function on the inherited structures. It does not install or quantify a new MetricSpace distance, identify c with a geodesic or path-length distance, assert path existence, or assert a Wasserstein or transport API result.
objects: Finite-dimensional real inner-product normed space E with its Borel measurable structure; exact unit subtype S; ambient representatives of subtype points; the actual principal-arccos function c on S times S; the actual inner-product angle of ambient vectors; and the ambient chord norm.
domains: E has NormedAddCommGroup, InnerProductSpace R, FiniteDimensional R, MeasurableSpace, and BorelSpace structures. S={w:E | norm(w)=1} inherits its topology and measurable structure; S times S uses their product structures. c:S times S->R. Unit representatives have norm 1 and inner products in [-1,1]. u,v,w range over S, with their ambient representatives in E. There is no positive-dimensionality premise, chosen geodesic space, probability measure, or measure-coupling domain.
quantifiers: For every E with the displayed structures, let S and c be fixed by the formulas. Conclude Continuous(c), Measurable(c), the conjunction of six listed pairwise properties for every u,v:S, and the triangle inequality for every u,v,w:S. The unit conditions are built into the subtype, not extra hypotheses restricting otherwise arbitrary vectors after quantification. No existential constants, curves, distances, or optimizers are quantified.
assumptions: Only the displayed real inner-product normed, finite-dimensional, and Borel measurable-space structures on E. S is defined by norm=1 and c by the literal arccos of the inner product. No continuity, measurability, nonnegativity, bound, angle identity, comparison, zero separation, symmetry, or triangle inequality is supplied as an assumption; all are produced conclusions. There is no nonempty sphere or dimension lower bound beyond finite dimensionality.
conclusion: c is jointly continuous and measurable. For every u,v:S, 0<=c(u,v)<=pi, c(u,v)=angle(u_bar,v_bar), norm_E(u_bar-v_bar)<=c(u,v), (c(u,v)=0 iff u=v), and c(u,v)=c(v,u). For every u,v,w:S, c(u,w)<=c(u,v)+c(v,w). These are exactly properties of the explicitly defined scalar function, with its ambient-angle and chord relations.
scopes: Continuity and measurability refer to the displayed c under the inherited subtype and product structures. The norm in the chord comparison is the ambient E norm, and the angle is the actual real-inner-product angle, not a newly introduced path metric. Its norm-product denominator equals 1 for these representatives, so totalized division causes no exceptional unit case. Zero-cost equality compares subtype points and hence ambient vectors. The function is not substituted for an independently chosen MetricSpace distance in this statement, nor is a new metric instance installed. No path/geodesic existence, length-minimization identification, or Wasserstein/transport assertion is included. Empty S is permitted, making the pointwise universal assertions vacuous. Completeness is not separately assumed and is a consequence of finite dimensionality over R, but no completeness conclusion for a newly defined metric is asserted.
constant_dependencies: The exact radius condition is norm=1. The scalar range is [0,pi] with the literal constant pi independent of dimension and points. The chord comparison has factor 1 and the triangle inequality has no extra factor. The actual function depends only on the fixed real inner product and unit representatives. There is no unspecified bound, dimension-dependent estimate, scale normalization, existential constant, or transport exponent.
